topic: Commissioning timeline and sponsor restructuring (status as of mid-2026)
wiki_text: As of mid-2026 the Puerto Sandino FSRU import terminal remains under construction. New Fortress Energy's first-quarter-2026 investor update (March 2026) listed Nicaragua terminal commissioning among its 2026 growth initiatives, targeting October 2026 - roughly five years after the project's original 2021 in-service goal and following repeated slips (2H2021, then Q4 2024, then Q1 2025). The associated 300 MW Puerto Sandino power plant has been reported as essentially complete; remaining work centers on the maritime/jetty and pipeline scope and final FSRU deployment. NFE has reported binding long-term LNG supply for the project from two U.S. liquefaction facilities (20-year terms commencing 2027 and 2029). Concurrently, NFE is undertaking a major creditor-led debt restructuring (~US$5.7bn) under a UK legal framework and intends to split into a publicly traded 'New NFE' that would own its Nicaragua, Puerto Rico and Mexico assets, including Puerto Sandino.

Reporting on the Puerto Sandino regasification vessel is not fully consistent. In November 2024 NFE CEO Wes Edens described the 125,856-cbm 'Energos Freeze' as the FSRU for Puerto Sandino (then completing work at the Navantia yard in El Ferrol, Spain, and due to deploy on exiting dry dock). Other coverage references the 138,000-cbm 'Energos Princess' serving as the floating storage unit (FSU) at the jetty, implying a possible two-vessel FSU+FSRU arrangement. GEM currently records the floating vessel as 'Energos Princess'. The deployed regas vessel name and IMO should be confirmed from NFE IR / vessel tracking before the GEM vessel field is changed.
